policy_presence.summary: CUHK leaves pedagogical AI rules to course teacher discretion. For example, Chung Chi College General Education courses (GECC3130/4130, AY2026/27) adopt Approach 2 ('Use only with prior permission'), where GenAI is prohibited for drafting written assignments but permitted for spelling and grammar checking, subject to approval by the Senate Committee on General Education. University-wide full student guide rules remain unverified behind ADFS SSO.

ai_disclosure.summary: In verified course outlines (GECC4130, AY2026/27), students must submit a signed academic honesty declaration confirming awareness of university regulations and acknowledging investigation by AI detection software (VeriGuide AWD). A university-wide declaration or prompt-logging rule has not been established in public evidence because the Student Guide to Academic Honesty remains restricted behind ADFS SSO.

coursework.summary: Instructors determine course-level AI policy. In verified General Education courses (GECC3130/4130, AY2026/27), Approach 2 is enforced: drafting is prohibited, spelling/grammar checking is allowed (subject to Senate General Education approval), and AI Index > 25% may receive a failing course grade.

exams.summary: This review has not established a university-wide AI rule for formal examinations because the central Student Guide to Academic Honesty remains gated behind ADFS SSO; invigilator instructions govern in-person exams.

privacy_data_entry.summary: CUHK's Enterprise AI Hub instructs users not to enter personal data, confidential information, restricted research data or other protected University information unless the specific service and use case have been approved for that data. Separately, ITSC directs users to check the enterprise data protection indicator and advises not entering personal or private information. Public unapproved platforms remain strictly prohibited for protected data.

academic_integrity.summary: Unauthorized AI usage constitutes academic dishonesty (plagiarism or unauthorized assistance) under Senate policy (effective AY2025-26, updated July 2026), with penalties from zero marks to expulsion. Disciplinary committees handle cases with procedural fairness, and students may appeal within 7 working days.

approved_tools.summary: Centrally provisioned tools include Microsoft Copilot Chat (Basic, free for all students/staff with institutional sign-in) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium, centrally allocated to eligible teaching staff and management; other units require departmental funding). CUHK AI Chatbot learning/teaching services are legacy services scheduled for retirement on 31 January 2027 for transition only. Generative AI API Portal access requires application, use-case review, and funding/quota. Perplexity Enterprise is planned but not currently available.

named_ai_services.summary: Centrally provisioned tools feature commercial data protection under institutional licensing; legacy chatbots remain active until 31 January 2027.

teaching_guidance.summary: University guidelines emphasize pedagogical alignment, human-in-the-loop oversight, and assessment design adaptations.

research_guidance.summary: CUHK Library's AI education and research guide links to 'Guidelines on the Responsible Use of AI for Research' in Schedule 11 of the Research Policy, marked as requiring login for staff and RPG students; this review has not retrieved that text and does not establish substantive research rules.

security_procurement.summary: CUHK ITSC and the Enterprise AI Hub provide access governance for approved institutional services and the Generative AI API Portal, which requires application, use-case review, and security review. Public evidence does not establish a universal procurement authorization mandate for all AI across the university.
